newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Taiwan's Chang urges S.Africa to protect investors.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Chang urges S.Africa to protect investors.

text.p: Taiwanese Foreign Minister John Chang urged Pretoria on Monday to negotiate a diplomatic status with Taipei strong enough to assure Taipei's business leaders their investments in South Africa would be safeguarded.

Chang told reporters during a brief stop at Johannesburg's airport that Taiwanese investors were jittery over South Africa's decision late last year to cut off formal ties with Taipei in favour of mainland China from December 1997.

"They became nervous about the future of investment," said Chang, speaking during a stop en route to Malawi and Swaziland. He returns on January 19 for talks with South African Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo to map out a future relationship.

Chang said he would not call for an investor pullout from South Africa, but cautioned that Pretoria needed to offer his government sufficient representation in the country to ensure Taiwanese business interests were protected.
"We will not take any action to pull them (investors) out, but it will be very difficult for us if they see the future arrangement of our relationship does not fit their needs.
"If they cannot keep confidence here, if our government's presence here is not strong enough, they will leave by themselves. They will depart if they do not feel safe," Chang said.
Nearly 300 Taiwan businesses have operations in South Africa with total investment topping $1.5 billion. At least 43,000 jobs are created through Taiwanese investment.

Referring to mainland China, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province and has tried to isolate it diplomatically, Chang told the South African government he wanted Beijing's influence to be limited in talks over future ties:

"We don't think mainland China should have a say...We hope the South African government can have an understanding of this. It's very important -- We don't think any sovereign state should be dictated to by any third party."

The tie-switching announcement by South Africa late last year was a big blow to Taiwan, which now has only 29 minor diplomatic allies. Its relations with Taiwan date back to the apartheid era when both were diplomatic pariahs.
Chang is on a seven-nation African tour hoping to shore up diplomatic ties on the continent. He is scheduled to return to Taiwan on February 2.
